title: Chapter 2909 - 161: Divine Slave (Part 3)
content:
Chapter 2909: Chapter 161: Divine Slave (Part 3)

As long as you believe in the Divine Lord, regardless of status, you are not allowed to be arbitrarily killed or harmed.

Upper-level Barbarian Cultivators may not casually kill, bully, insult, or disgrace ordinary tribal Barbarian Cultivators, or they will face punishment from the Divine Lord.

All Barbarian Cultivators have the right to learn Tao Cultivation.

All Barbarian Cultivators should be loyal to their tribes.

Within the tribes, all Barbarian Cultivators who believe in the Divine Lord should unite, cherish, and coexist harmoniously...

...

Such concepts, originally impossible to achieve in the Barbaric Wilderness, were covertly transformed by Mo Hua, infusing them with the "faith" in the Divine Lord, and forcibly implemented using divine authority.

The majority of Barbarian Cultivators are ignorant, brutal, greedy, and self-seeking.

Normal "civilization" is simply impossible.

Mo Hua had no way to make these Barbarian Cultivators pursue fairness, justice, truth, or kindness.

The word "morality" does not exist in their world; no amount of explanation or advocacy can make them understand.

Even if they do understand, by the time they realize this amidst their internal struggles for fame and profit, it would be too late.

The great calamity had already descended, and everyone in the Barbaric Wilderness would perish.

Therefore, the only means is to use "faith," almost similar to "superstition," to govern the form of Divine Sense.

Using "faith" to shape their Taoist Heart.

Everything is the Divine Lord’s directive; everything is the Divine Lord’s prophecy.

Faith is everything.

Barbarian Cultivators in the Wilderness need only follow suit.

This is almost the only method Mo Hua could conceive and execute.

It is also the sole ray of hope amidst the ominous destiny of the Heavenly Dao in the Great Wilderness.

Simultaneously, Mo Hua also went along with the tide to do what he had long wanted to do, but had never had the strength to accomplish:

Liberate the Barbarian Slaves.

All the Barbarian Slaves of the Great Wilderness are no longer subordinate to any tribe or force, but are unified under the name of the "Divine Lord."

They are no longer human slaves but now slaves to the divine.

And all Barbarian Slaves, gathering together, reconstitute a large tribe, known as the "Divine Slave Tribe."

Mo Hua originally did not like using this name either.

He disliked the word "slave," and his original intent was for all Barbarian Slaves in the Great Wilderness to gain freedom.

But from a practical standpoint, this wish is too advanced; at least now, it’s simply impossible.

In the Barbaric Wilderness, Barbarian Slaves are indeed miserable.

But what is even more miserable is a Barbarian Slave without a master.

A Barbarian Slave without a master means being a slave to everyone.

Since they are "masterless," any tribe or individual can freely possess, bully, or even kill them.

If Mo Hua’s work in the Great Wilderness succeeds, the Barbarian Slaves can overturn their situation.

But if it fails, they would instantly revert to their original state.

In such a case, their plight would be even worse than before.

Therefore, Mo Hua must devise an escape route for them, leaving them with a "master."

Even if the final failure results in a harsher situation, these Barbarian Slaves can still rally under the name of "Divine Slaves."

No tribe would dare blatantly compete with the "Divine Lord" for Barbarian Slaves.

The term "Divine Slave" becomes their last amulet.

Idealism is beautiful; reality is cruel.

If you wish to change reality, you must first accept a portion of reality, then change another part.

Accept one part, then change another.

Bit by bit, step by step, through generations of relentless effort, only then can reality be transformed into the ideal...

Thus, Mo Hua, this Shaman, under the guise of the "Divine Lord," has completed the initial liberation of the Barbarian Slaves in the Great Wilderness.

And the Divine Slave Tribe has become the largest, most influential, and far-reaching force in the Great Wilderness, as well as the most devoted to the Divine Lord and to Mo Hua, the Shaman.

It is Mo Hua, in the name of the "Divine Lord," who liberated them.

They have nothing, except faith.

At the same time, it is precisely because they have nothing that they possess fearless courage and steadfast conviction.
